summary: The SOP is detailed, carefully labeled and mostly accurate against its sources, but its cutover and rollback mechanics have real safety gaps: inbound subscriptions from 14 lose their state, the read-only fence can be bypassed and blocks the DBA's own steps, and the rollback decision time ignores Cloud SQL's cancel limits and the combined time budget. Several provider-specific facts it cites (PostGIS 3.6.0 not offered on Cloud SQL 14, output_plugin_libraries already live on 14.24 with no Cloud SQL flag) also change the path decision and the Block 1 order, and the SOP doesn't surface them.

findings.claim: For a subscriber instance, the SOP's only step is 'disable and re-enable' the inbound subscriptions. pg_upgrade from a pre-17 source silently drops each subscription's table states and replication origin, so after re-enabling, the subscription can't continue where it stopped. It may skip or re-copy data, and no gate checks inbound subscriptions (G2.5 covers only outbound CDC consumers).
findings.evidence: SOP line 71: 'A subscription means this instance also consumes from somewhere else, so it needs its own disable and re-enable steps in the runbook.' B1-05 (line 131) likewise says only 'the disable and re-enable steps for inbound subscriptions'. PostgreSQL 18 docs, Logical Replication > Upgrade (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/logical-replication-upgrade.html): 'pg_upgrade attempts to migrate subscription dependencies which includes the subscription's table information present in pg_subscription_rel system catalog and also the subscription's replication origin... Migration of subscription dependencies is only supported when the old cluster is version 17.0 or later. Subscription dependencies on clusters before version 17.0 will silently be ignored.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a runbook procedure for inbound subscriptions on a 14 source: record each origin LSN, then after the upgrade either recreate the subscription with copy_data=false and advance its origin, or re-sync with a planned truncate and copy. Add a gate that checks the subscriber data with sentinels or row counts after the rehearsal.

findings.claim: The T+10 rule says 'roll back unless the upgrade has finished' at the latest rollback decision time. On Cloud SQL, though, a restore can't start until the operation is cancelled or ends. Cancelling is impossible outside the main phase or when replicas are included, and a cancel isn't instantaneous. So at decision time the team may have to wait up to the six-hour timeout, and the rehearsed rollback duration doesn't include this wait or the cancel-and-revert time.
findings.evidence: SOP line 284: 'At the latest rollback decision time ... roll back unless the upgrade has finished ... Cloud SQL can cancel only during the main upgrade phase, and not when replicas are included [S-01]. A restore starts only after the operation is cancelled or has ended.' S-01 (live page): 'Cancellation isn't instantaneous. Triggering a cancellation doesn't immediately restore access to your instance. The instance remains unavailable while Cloud SQL performs the necessary rollback steps'; 'Upgrade operation : Returns a timeout error if not finished within six hours'; 'If you use read replicas and choose to include replicas with your major version upgrade , you can't cancel the major version upgrade.' S-01 also says an accepted cancel reverts the instance itself, a rollback path the SOP never times.
findings.suggested_fix: Rehearse and time a cancel-and-revert, and use it as the rollback when the upgrade is cancellable. State what to do when the operation can't be cancelled, and move the decision time earlier by the worst-case wait. When replicas are included, the decision record should accept that cutover has no cancel option.

findings.claim: No gate checks that the upgrade and validation, plus the rollback, fit in the window together. G2.1 checks only that the in-window steps take at most 75% of the window, and G2.6 only times the rollback. If the rehearsed upgrade ends after 'window end minus 1.25 times rollback', the decision time comes before the upgrade can finish, and the runbook forces a rollback every time.
findings.evidence: G2.1 (line 165): 'Two rehearsals in a row finish the in-window steps within 75% of the window'. Line 247: 'The latest rollback decision time is the window's end minus 1.25 times this duration.' No gate compares the rehearsed upgrade, validation and go or no-go 2 end time with that decision time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a G2 gate: the rehearsed time from T-0 through go or no-go 2, plus 1.25 times the rehearsed rollback (and any cancel wait), must fit inside the window. Show the arithmetic on the timing sheet.

findings.claim: The write fence is a database-level default that any session can override. Direct connections that skip the pooler (jobs, Auth Proxy clients) can reconnect and write to the upgraded instance before reopening. Those writes would be lost on rollback, but the SOP says rollback loses no data.
findings.evidence: SOP line 205: 'Set ALTER DATABASE <db> SET default_transaction_read_only = on for each app database, then end the remaining app sessions.' Line 300: 'Nothing was written after the fence ... so no data is lost. This holds only if the fence held (Inferred).' PG 18 SET TRANSACTION docs (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-set-transaction.html): 'SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS sets the default transaction characteristics for subsequent transactions of a session ... the defaults can be set in the configuration file, via ALTER DATABASE', so a client can issue SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE. The Cloud SQL release notes (2026-04-23) describe cloudsql_session_read_only as 'a robust, non-circumventable mechanism ... for preventing data modification during a session.'
findings.suggested_fix: Fence at the connection level: revoke CONNECT or set NOLOGIN on app roles, tighten authorized networks, or evaluate cloudsql_session_read_only=locked. Keep the fence on the upgraded instance until go or no-go 2, and verify it with the census query.

findings.claim: With default_transaction_read_only set on every app database, the DBA's own in-window steps fail. These include the final sentinel INSERT, ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... DISABLE at T+5, and ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE after the upgrade. The SOP never tells the DBA to override the setting in their own session.
findings.evidence: SOP line 207: 'Insert one final sentinel row' (after the read-only setting); line 219: 'run ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE for each pending extension'; Block 3 T+5: 'disable inbound subscriptions'. PG 18 docs (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-set-transaction.html): 'When a transaction is read-only, the following SQL commands are disallowed: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ... all CREATE, ALTER, and DROP commands'.
findings.suggested_fix: Before each DBA step that writes or runs DDL inside the fence, add an explicit 'SET default_transaction_read_only = off' (or BEGIN READ WRITE) for the DBA session. List which steps need it.

findings.claim: The drain test depends on the sentinel reaching each consumer and on confirmed_flush_lsn having 'stopped advancing'. A stalled or crashed consumer also stops advancing. Slots whose consumers don't include the sentinel table, such as Datastream, pglogical or filtered Debezium, have no sentinel check. The fence LSN the SOP records is never compared. Because the MVU deletes every slot, an undrained slot means downstream data loss.
findings.evidence: Line 207: 'Insert one final sentinel row, and note pg_current_wal_lsn().' Line 210: 'A consumer is drained when the final sentinel has arrived downstream and its slot's confirmed_flush_lsn stopped advancing across two checks a minute apart'. S-01: 'deletes all existing logical replication slots on the instance'.
findings.suggested_fix: Define 'drained' as confirmed_flush_lsn at or above the recorded fence LSN for every logical slot, with the sentinel as an extra check. Require each production publication and connector include list to contain the sentinel table, or name the slots where that isn't possible.

findings.claim: The SOP says Cloud SQL 18 needs PostGIS 3.6.0 but doesn't mention that Cloud SQL's PostgreSQL 14 offers only 3.5.2. The prerequisite can't be met in place on the source, so a PostGIS user may face a blocked 14-to-18 MVU, a two-hop upgrade, or a provider exception. That affects the path decision in G0.6.
findings.evidence: SOP line 83: 'Cloud SQL 18 needs PostGIS 3.6.0, and pg_squeeze 1.8 [S-01].' S-01: 'For PostgreSQL 18, upgrade to PostGIS version 3.6.0.' S-10 (live page): 'PostgreSQL 14 3.5.2 ... PostgreSQL 17 3.5.2 PostgreSQL 18 3.6.0'.
findings.suggested_fix: Flag this conflict between S-01 and S-10 as Unverified, add it to appendix B, and require the provider precheck or a clone rehearsal to settle it before the decision record picks the path and target for PostGIS users.

findings.claim: The SOP treats output_plugin_libraries as a target-version concern ('allowed on the target'), but the restriction applies to the source as soon as it runs 14.24. Cloud SQL has already rolled out 14.24 and documents no output_plugin_libraries flag. Non-pgoutput CDC such as wal2json or decoderbufs may break on production in Block 1, while appendix B question 3 isn't required to be answered until Block 2 exits.
findings.evidence: B1-03: 'plan how decoding plugins will be allowed on the target [S-21]'. S-21: 'By default, only the output plugins shipped as part of PostgreSQL ( pgoutput and test_decoding ) are included in output_plugin_libraries . Installations that rely on other output plugins must add them after updating the server'. S-09 release notes, 2026-11-03: 'Minor versions 14.23 is upgraded to 14.24.' S-11 supports: 'The page has no output_plugin_libraries entry' (confirmed live: 0 hits).
findings.suggested_fix: Make question 3 a Block 0 item, tied to G0.5. Check each non-pgoutput CDC slot on the source now, and before B1-13 applies any minor update.

findings.claim: Rollback moves traffic to a new recovery instance, which has a new IP and connection name and probably a new server CA. The rehearsal can't time repointing production apps, because they can't be pointed at a clone. Apps that connect directly or pin server certificates need config or secret changes during a deploy freeze. The rollback timing that sets the decision time therefore leaves out its slowest step.
findings.evidence: Line 244: 'Repoint the pooler, apps and CDC, creating new slots on the recovery instance.' Rollback (line 297): 'Repoint the pooler and apps.' S-06: 'The new instance has a new IP address or addresses.' Block 3 entry: 'A migration and deploy freeze ... in place.'
findings.suggested_fix: From the G0.1 consumer rows, list every consumer that connects without the pooler and how it gets repointed (DNS, secret, deploy), and get a deploy-freeze exception for rollback. Time a dry run of those changes and add it to the rollback duration.

findings.claim: The SOP has no check for collation-library version changes between the 14 and 18 images. pg_upgrade keeps existing index files, so a glibc or ICU change can silently corrupt text indexes. Standard practice compares collation versions and reindexes the affected indexes, and appendix B doesn't ask the provider about it.
findings.evidence: B1-14 covers only btree_gist and ltree, FTS and pg_trgm on non-libc clusters, and nondeterministic PK and FK pairs. There's no query comparing pg_collation.collversion with pg_collation_actual_version(), and no appendix B question about the glibc or ICU version in Cloud SQL's 14 and 18 images. I couldn't find a public Cloud SQL source on this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a kit section listing collations with their recorded and actual versions on the source and the clone after the upgrade, plus an appendix B question about the OS collation library. Reindex affected text indexes as a timed runbook step if versions differ.

findings.claim: The kit's per-database loop gives the connection both as a positional argument and with -d. psql then reads the positional connection string as the username, so following the documented loop fails to produce the per-database files G0.2 requires. Also, a connection failure prints 'psql: error' or 'FATAL', which the SOP's search for 'ERROR' misses.
findings.evidence: precheck.sql line 25: 'psql "<connection>" -d "$db" -X -f precheck.sql > "precheck-$db.txt" 2>&1'. psql 18 docs (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/app-psql.html): synopsis 'psql [ option ...] [ dbname [ username ]]' and '-d dbname ... This is equivalent to specifying dbname as the first non-option argument'. SOP line 66: 'Search each file for ERROR and permission denied.'
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single conninfo that includes the database, for example psql "<connection> dbname=$db", or put the connection only in -d. Add a case-insensitive search for 'error' and 'FATAL', or require the section 0 header, to the validation step.

findings.claim: The live consumer census, which G0.1 and the fence check depend on, has no query, sampling cadence, or required privilege. Point-in-time samples of pg_stat_activity miss short-lived connections such as cron jobs, and agents can't run the samples. A new team can't run it as written.
findings.evidence: B0-06: 'Live consumer census: group pg_stat_activity by user and application, sampled over a week'. Line 206: 'Confirm with the census query that only expected sessions remain' (no census query is defined anywhere). Kit 4c notes 'needs pg_read_all_stats to see other users'.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the census query in the kit, state the role it needs (pg_read_all_stats) and the sampling schedule a person runs. Add connection logging (log_connections or Cloud SQL audit logs) to catch short-lived clients.

findings.claim: G1.4 makes a full password rotation a Block 1 exit gate, but the SOP itself says PG 18 still accepts MD5 logins. Rotating every password-login role in production is a risky credential rollout that the upgrade doesn't require, and the gate doesn't require coordinating the rollout with each consumer.
findings.evidence: Line 98: 'PG 18 deprecates MD5 passwords but still accepts MD5 logins, and only warns when an MD5 password is set [S-17].' S-17: 'Support for MD5 passwords will be removed in a future major version release. CREATE ROLE and ALTER ROLE now emit deprecation warnings when setting MD5 passwords.'
findings.suggested_fix: Mark G1.4 as not an upgrade blocker, or allow a default waiver. Where rotation is done, require a per-consumer secret rollout plan and driver SCRAM check before each reset.

findings.claim: Some gates can close on someone's say-so. For G0.1, the evidence of an owner's confirmation isn't defined. For G0.7, the evidence 'question rows with an owner' doesn't prove the questions were sent.
findings.evidence: G0.1: 'Consumer rows with an owner who has confirmed them'. G0.7: 'Questions for the provider have been sent ... | Question rows with an owner'.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a link to each owner's confirming reply for G0.1, and the support case or email link for G0.7.

findings.claim: After reopening, the SOP's only option is fix-forward, and it says to have the business approver sign that in the decision record. The G0.6 list of decision-record contents doesn't include this sign-off, and reverse logical replication from 18 back to a 14 recovery instance isn't considered as a fallback.
findings.evidence: Line 302: 'Plan to fix forward, and have the business approver sign that in the decision record.' G0.6 (line 42) lists 'rollback approach and its latest decision time' but not acceptance of post-reopen data-loss or fix-forward.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'post-reopen fix-forward acceptance, signed by the business approver' to G0.6. Mention reverse logical replication as an option the decision record weighs explicitly.

findings.claim: Appendix A cites the 14.24 notes for output_plugin_libraries and btree_gist and ltree. It leaves out the pgcrypto change in the same notes, which makes PGP data encrypted with an unsupported cipher fail to decrypt by default. That is one of the 'data cleanups' the notes say may be needed.
findings.evidence: S-21 (live): 'the first three security entries below describe configuration adjustments and data cleanups that you may need to make after updating' and 'By default, pgcrypto will now fail to decrypt any messages that were affected in this way. To allow retrieval of such data, a new option ignore-cipher-failure has been added'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 14.24 row for pgcrypto PGP ciphers (owner: app teams using pgp_sym_decrypt or pgp_pub_decrypt), and a readiness-scan hazard for these functions.

findings.claim: The SOP says its sources were rechecked live, but sources.md still marks S-10 as 'changed', and the SOP cites S-10 as Verified. S-34 to S-37 have no lastChecked, status or verified fields in sources.json and no rows in sources.md, although G1.4, B1-13, B1-15 and the XID guidance depend on them. I confirmed live that their quotes are present.
findings.evidence: SOP line 3: 'Sources were rechecked live on that date ([sources.md](sources.md)).' sources.md: 'S-10 ... | changed 2026-11-04', with the rule 'Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks.' In sources.json (around line 620), the S-34 entry has only id, title, url, supports and quotes. The S-10 quote 'they don't automatically update the extension's database catalog' is present on the live page.
findings.suggested_fix: Rerun check-sources.mjs --write so S-10's status is updated and S-34 to S-37 get dates and rows in sources.md. Until then, label the S-10 claims Unverified.

findings.claim: The SOP says search_path-dependent functions in generated columns and CHECK constraints can fail, but S-18 names only expression indexes and materialized views. Kit section 6g doesn't check CHECK constraints at all, so readers may believe they're covered.
findings.evidence: Line 80: 'a function used in an index, materialized view, generated column or CHECK constraint that relies on search_path can fail.' S-18: 'Functions used by expression indexes and materialized views that need to reference non-default schemas must specify a search path'. precheck.sql 6g (line 188) covers 'indexes, matviews or generated columns' only, with no pg_constraint branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the generated-column and CHECK cases Inferred, and either add a pg_constraint branch to 6g or remove CHECK from the SOP text.

findings.claim: The in-window analyze uses 'vacuumdb --all' while also requiring every step to run as the database owner. With databases owned by different roles, one role can't own them all. --all also tries every connectable database, which may include provider-internal ones the role can't reach.
findings.evidence: Line 220: 'Run every step as the database owner ... ANALYZE silently skips tables the caller can't analyze [S-16].' Line 234: 'run vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages inside the window.' Line 235: 'time a full vacuumdb --all --analyze-only'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace --all with one vacuumdb -d <db> per customer database, each run as that database's owner, and rerun the coverage query per database to prove nothing was skipped.

findings.claim: G2.5 requires each sentinel to arrive downstream exactly once. Common connectors such as Debezium deliver at-least-once and can resend events after a restart, so a correct cutover may fail this gate, which pushes teams toward waivers.
findings.evidence: G2.5: 'sentinel rows written before the fence and after the new slots were created each arrived downstream exactly once.'
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'at least once, with no gaps', and let each CDC owner state whether duplicates are acceptable or are removed downstream.

findings.claim: Replica handling covers only read replicas that are upgraded with the primary or first. It leaves out external replicas, which Cloud SQL can't upgrade in place, and cross-region DR replicas. HA (regional) configuration isn't part of the clone's shape in G2.1.
findings.evidence: S-01: 'You can't perform an in-place major version upgrade on an external replica .' G2.1 (line 165) matches the clone on 'tier, storage, replica topology and minor version' and doesn't mention HA.
findings.suggested_fix: Add external and cross-region replicas to the G0.6 replica-handling choices with a rebuild plan, and include HA configuration in the G2.1 clone shape.
